title: A Spectral Threshold That Predicts When LoRA Will Forget
hook: LoRA sometimes injects 'intruder dimensions' that trigger catastrophic forgetting. This paper predicts the per-layer update strength where they appear, from the pretrained spectrum alone.
key_points: Intruder dimensions are new leading singular vectors of W+BA that are nearly orthogonal to every pretrained singular vector, and they drive catastrophic forgetting.
The paper derives a per-layer critical update strength from the measured spectrum of W alone, via the rectangular spiked-deformation transform, with no fitted parameters.

Across four dense Transformer families, a state-space model, an MoE, and an encoder-decoder — 18 adapters, 9,840 layer scans — it localizes the empirical threshold within a factor of two on 82% of layers.
It separates intruder-bearing from intruder-free layers at deployment with mean AUC 0.89, and holds unchanged on six third-party adapters.
It resolves the LoRA-vs-full-fine-tuning asymmetry: full fine-tuning disperses its update far below every layer's threshold.

Norm-matched interventions show threshold-crossing layers, not update magnitude, carry the forgetting; a spike-budget rule needing one SVD cuts forgetting 62% on the most fragile model at no task cost.
content_html: LoRA's failure mode has a name and a cause. Fine-tuning with a low-rank update can produce intruder dimensions — new leading singular vectors of the updated weight matrix W+BA that sit nearly orthogonal to every pretrained singular vector — and those are what tip a model into catastrophic forgetting. Since that discovery, nobody could predict, layer by layer, when they would show up. This paper does.
extra_html:
The law

Xie derives a per-layer critical update strength computed from the measured spectrum of W alone, using the rectangular spiked-deformation transform, together with an exact secular-equation characterization of the updated spectrum. There are no fitted parameters — it's a prediction from the pretrained weights, not a curve fit to observed failures.

The validation is pre-specified and broad: four dense Transformer families, a state-space model, a mixture-of-experts model, and an encoder-decoder, spanning 18 adapters and 9,840 layer scans. The law localizes the empirical threshold within a factor of two on 82% of layers, separates intruder-bearing from intruder-free layers with a mean AUC of 0.89, holds unchanged on six third-party adapters, and predicts where WikiText-2 perplexity starts degrading.

Why LoRA and full fine-tuning differ

The framework also explains the asymmetry people have observed for years: full fine-tuning disperses its update far below the threshold of every layer, so it never crosses. Norm-matched interventions confirm that it's threshold-crossing rather than update magnitude that carries the forgetting. That yields a cheap fix — a spike-budget rule derived from the thresholds, requiring a single SVD and no validation sweeps, which reduced forgetting by 62% on the most fragile model at no cost to task performance.

related.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation
related.hook: Why retrain billions of weights when you can freeze them all and train tiny add-on matrices instead? LoRA tunes under ~1% of the parameters with near-full-fine-tune quality.

related.title: Not Every LoRA Matrix Is Worth Updating
related.hook: LoRA trains every matrix equally hard. A matrix's condition number reveals which ones actually drive adaptation — tune the top half and you keep the accuracy for half the parameters.

related.title: QLoRA: Fine-tuning Quantized LLMs
related.hook: Fine-tune a model with tens of billions of parameters on a single GPU. QLoRA squeezes the frozen base to 4-bit, then trains LoRA adapters on top — without losing quality.

related.title: How Many Bits Can a LoRA Adapter Write?
related.hook: Everyone treats a LoRA adapter as a skill, not a record of its training data. Weighed in bits, it stores a couple per trainable parameter — and where you put them matters more than how many.

flashcards.prompt: What is an 'intruder dimension' in a LoRA-tuned model?
flashcards.back_html: A new leading singular vector of the updated matrix W+BA that is nearly orthogonal to all of the pretrained singular vectors. Their appearance is what drives catastrophic forgetting.

flashcards.prompt: Why does full fine-tuning avoid the forgetting that LoRA can cause, per this paper?

choices.text: It disperses its update across directions, staying far below every layer's critical threshold
It uses a much smaller effective learning rate than LoRA does
It updates the singular values but never the singular vectors

flashcards.explanation_html: The threshold is about concentration, not size. LoRA's low-rank update can concentrate enough strength in one direction to cross a layer's critical value; a full-rank update spreads the same magnitude out and never does.

flashcards.prompt: What did norm-matched interventions establish about the source of forgetting?
flashcards.back_html: That crossing the threshold, not the raw magnitude of the update, is what carries the forgetting — layers matched on update norm behaved very differently depending on whether they crossed.
